_comment: Source of truth for chaos trigger definitions. src/scripts/crash-injector/sweep-chaos.sh reads this file. Tiers 1-4 are established scenarios; tier 5 is explicitly experimental/unsupported and must not be treated as validated RHOV behavior. Scripts read this file; do not duplicate these entries elsewhere.

tierSchema.5: experimental/unsupported mechanisms; explicit operator opt-in required

nmi-inject.name: NMI injection
nmi-inject.note: Delivers a hardware NMI to the guest vCPU via virsh inject-nmi. VERIFIED 2026-08-26: Windows Server 2025 handles the NMI gracefully without bug-checking. The HAL NMI handler absorbs the interrupt.

balloon-squeeze.name: Memory balloon squeeze under load
balloon-squeeze.note: Shrinks guest memory from 8 GB to 1 GB via virtio balloon while the guest allocates memory. VERIFIED 2026-08-26: Windows Server 2025 memory manager handles the pressure gracefully; no BSOD produced.

storage-hotremove.name: Boot disk hot-remove during I/O
storage-hotremove.note: Removes the boot disk (vda) while the guest is doing I/O. VERIFIED 2026-08-26: virtio-blk hot-unplug is clean; Windows continues from cached pages and the guest stays up. No BSOD produced.

network-toggle.name: Network link toggle under load
network-toggle.guestWorkload: 1..10000 | ForEach-Object { try { Invoke-WebRequest -Uri http://10.0.2.2 -TimeoutSec 1 -UseBasicParsing -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue } catch {} }
network-toggle.note: Toggles the virtio-net link down then up during network I/O. VERIFIED 2026-08-26: netkvm handles disconnect gracefully as expected; no BSOD. Resilience validated.

vcpu-hotremove.name: vCPU hot-remove
vcpu-hotremove.note: Reduces vCPUs from 4 to 1 while the guest is running. VERIFIED 2026-08-26: Domain CPU topology (4 sockets, no hotpluggable vCPUs) prevents hot-remove; virsh setvcpus fails with 'failed to find appropriate hotpluggable vcpus'. Requires maxvcpus > vcpus in domain XML for hotplug.

verifier-lowres.name: Driver Verifier Low Resources Simulation
verifier-lowres.guestWorkload: Get-ChildItem C:\ -Recurse -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Out-Null; Get-Process | Out-Null; Get-Service | Out-Null; ipconfig /all | Out-Null
verifier-lowres.note: VERIFIED 2026-08-26: VM crashed at 356s. Dirty shutdown confirmed (System/6008). LiveKernelEvent code 0x1a8 logged but NO traditional BugCheck System/1001 event. No crash dump written. The crash bypassed the normal crash dump mechanism, revealing a detection gap: the detector must also check LiveKernelEvent and 6008 dirty shutdown events.

verifier-forced-pending.name: Driver Verifier Forced Pending I/O
verifier-forced-pending.note: Runs with Driver Verifier Forced Pending I/O + IRP Logging enabled. VERIFIED 2026-08-26: No crash after 3027s. The workload (100 reads of ntoskrnl.exe) completed without triggering any IRP verification failures. virtio-blk and vioscsi handle forced-pending I/O correctly.

blkdeviotune.name: Block I/O throttle to near-zero
blkdeviotune.note: Throttles disk I/O to near-zero via virsh blkdeviotune while the guest performs heavy reads. VERIFIED 2026-08-26: I/O throttle makes SSH unresponsive (false crash detection) but does NOT produce a BSOD. Framebuffer capture confirmed the VM stays at the lock screen. The throttle must be removed before virsh reset or the VM hangs on reboot.

blkdebug-config.name: QEMU blkdebug read error injection
blkdebug-config.note: VERIFIED 2026-08-26: No BSOD. Tested three approaches: (1) runtime read-only EIO injection via QMP blockdev-add/blockdev-reopen after boot; SSH drops but framebuffer shows lock screen, no crash. (2) Boot-time injection; VM hangs at black screen (UEFI can't read disk), no BSOD. (3) Full read+write+flush EIO under heavy workload (Get-ChildItem + 50MB writes + memory pressure) for 300s; VM stays at lock screen, no crash. Windows Server 2025 NTFS and virtio-blk handle EIO gracefully without bug-checking. QMP runtime injection (blockdev-add + blockdev-reopen) works without domain XML changes.

enlightenment-no-tlbflush-ipi.name: Hyper-V without tlbflush+ipi enlightenments
enlightenment-no-tlbflush-ipi.guestWorkload: 1..50 | ForEach-Object { Start-Job -ScriptBlock { Get-Process | Out-Null } | Out-Null }; Get-Job | Wait-Job -Timeout 60 | Out-Null
enlightenment-no-tlbflush-ipi.note: Boots with tlbflush and ipi enlightenments disabled (the validated HYPERVISOR_ERROR mitigation). VERIFIED 2026-08-26: stable under workload for 627s. Mitigation confirmed sufficient.

enlightenment-no-vapic.name: Hyper-V without vapic enlightenment
enlightenment-no-vapic.guestWorkload: 1..50 | ForEach-Object { Start-Job -ScriptBlock { Get-Process | Out-Null } | Out-Null }; Get-Job | Wait-Job -Timeout 60 | Out-Null
enlightenment-no-vapic.note: Boots with vapic enlightenment disabled. VERIFIED 2026-08-26: stable under workload for 545s. Low risk classification in host-signals.json confirmed.

enlightenment-minimal.name: Hyper-V minimal enlightenments
enlightenment-minimal.guestWorkload: 1..50 | ForEach-Object { Start-Job -ScriptBlock { Get-Process | Out-Null } | Out-Null }; Get-Job | Wait-Job -Timeout 60 | Out-Null
enlightenment-minimal.note: Boots with only essential Hyper-V enlightenments (relaxed, vpindex, runtime, synic, reset, frequencies, spinlocks). VERIFIED 2026-08-26: stable under workload for 522s. Maximum enlightenment reduction is viable.

mce-uncorrectable.name: Machine Check Exception (uncorrectable)
mce-uncorrectable.note: Injects an uncorrectable MCE with PCC (Processor Context Corrupt) via QMP human-monitor-command. VERIFIED 2026-08-26: VM crashed at 16s. LiveKernelEvent 0x1a8 logged but no traditional BugCheck or crash dump. Same bypass pattern as verifier-lowres. MCE is severe enough to kill the crash dump path itself.

critical-process-kill.name: Critical process termination (csrss.exe)
critical-process-kill.guestWorkload: wmic recoveryos set AutoReboot = False 2>$null | Out-Null; Add-Type 'using System;using System.Runtime.InteropServices;public class P{[DllImport("kernel32.dll",SetLastError=true)]public static extern IntPtr OpenProcess(uint a,bool b,int c);[DllImport("kernel32.dll",SetLastError=true)]public static extern bool TerminateProcess(IntPtr h,uint e);}';$pid=(Get-Process csrss)[0].Id;$h=[P]::OpenProcess(0x0001,$false,$pid);[P]::TerminateProcess($h,1)
critical-process-kill.note: VERIFIED 2026-08-26: No crash. taskkill refuses critical processes. P/Invoke TerminateProcess on session-1 csrss drops SSH but system recovers in 5s (no reboot). TerminateProcess on both csrss instances returns False. Windows Server 2025 protects csrss from user-mode termination even with SeDebugPrivilege.

pause-resume-desync.name: VM pause/resume clock desync
pause-resume-desync.guestWorkload: 1..50 | ForEach-Object { Start-Job -ScriptBlock { Get-Process | Out-Null } | Out-Null }; Get-Job | Wait-Job -Timeout 60 | Out-Null
pause-resume-desync.note: VERIFIED 2026-08-26: No crash. QMP stop/cont with 20s pause completed cleanly. kvmclock and reenlightenment correction properly compensated for the time gap. Guest survived without watchdog timeout.

verifier-special-pool.name: Driver Verifier Special Pool + Low Resources
verifier-special-pool.guestWorkload: Get-ChildItem C:\Windows\System32 -Recurse -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Out-Null; 1..200 | ForEach-Object { Get-Content C:\Windows\System32\ntoskrnl.exe -ReadCount 0 -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Out-Null }
verifier-special-pool.note: VERIFIED 2026-08-26: VM crashed at 338s. Actual flags applied: 0x616 (Force IRQL + Low Resources + Force Pending + IRP Logging + I/O Verification). Dirty shutdown confirmed. Same bypass pattern as verifier-lowres (no traditional BugCheck dump).

verifier-systematic-lowres.name: Driver Verifier Systematic Low Resources
verifier-systematic-lowres.guestWorkload: Get-ChildItem C:\ -Recurse -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Out-Null; Get-Process | Out-Null; 1..100 | ForEach-Object { [IO.File]::WriteAllBytes("C:\chaos-test-$_.dat", [byte[]]::new(10MB)) }
verifier-systematic-lowres.note: VERIFIED 2026-08-26: VM crashed at 190s. Systematic Low Resources + Low Resources + Force Pending + IRP Logging + I/O Verification. Crashed faster than random mode (190s vs 356s for verifier-lowres). No traditional BugCheck dump.

verifier-deadlock-lowres.name: Driver Verifier Deadlock Detection + Low Resources
verifier-deadlock-lowres.guestWorkload: 1..50 | ForEach-Object { Start-Job -ScriptBlock { Get-ChildItem C:\ -Recurse -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Out-Null } | Out-Null }; Get-Job | Wait-Job -Timeout 120 | Out-Null; Get-Process | Out-Null; Get-Service | Out-Null
verifier-deadlock-lowres.note: VERIFIED 2026-08-26: VM crashed at 2s (during boot). Deadlock Detection + Low Resources + Force Pending + IRP Logging + I/O Verification. So aggressive the VM cannot survive boot; SSH never came up. Demonstrates severe lock ordering + allocation failure interaction.

verifier-ddi-compliance.name: Driver Verifier DDI Compliance + Low Resources
verifier-ddi-compliance.guestWorkload: Get-ChildItem C:\ -Recurse -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Out-Null; Get-Process | Out-Null; Get-Service | Out-Null; ipconfig /all | Out-Null; Get-NetAdapter | Out-Null
verifier-ddi-compliance.note: VERIFIED 2026-08-26: VM crashed at 229s. Actual flags: 0x8614 (Power Framework Delay Fuzzing + Low Resources + Force Pending + IRP Logging + I/O Verification). Note: 0x8000 is Power Framework, not DDI Compliance (0x20000). Crashed via power framework delays combined with allocation failures.

nonpaged-pool-exhaust.name: Nonpaged pool exhaustion via kernel objects
nonpaged-pool-exhaust.guestWorkload: Add-Type 'using System;using System.Runtime.InteropServices;public class K{[DllImport("kernel32.dll")]public static extern IntPtr CreateEvent(IntPtr a,bool b,bool c,string d);[DllImport("kernel32.dll")]public static extern IntPtr CreateSemaphore(IntPtr a,int b,int c,string d);}';while($true){$h=[K]::CreateEvent([IntPtr]::Zero,$true,$false,$null);$s=[K]::CreateSemaphore([IntPtr]::Zero,0,1,$null);if($h -eq [IntPtr]::Zero -and $s -eq [IntPtr]::Zero){break}};Get-Process|Out-Null
nonpaged-pool-exhaust.note: VERIFIED 2026-08-26: VM crashed at 44s. P/Invoke kernel object flood exhausted nonpaged pool rapidly. Unlike verifier-lowres (simulated failures), this causes REAL allocation failures affecting ALL drivers simultaneously. Fastest guest-side crash trigger.

thread-explosion.name: Kernel stack exhaustion via thread explosion
thread-explosion.note: VERIFIED 2026-08-26: No crash after 1021s. Windows Server 2025 scheduler handled 50K threads gracefully. Thread creation may have been throttled before kernel stack exhaustion occurred.

acpi-s3-under-io.name: ACPI S3 suspend during heavy I/O
acpi-s3-under-io.guestWorkload: $jobs = @(); $jobs += Start-Job { 1..10000 | ForEach-Object { [IO.File]::WriteAllBytes("C:\chaos-s3-$_.dat", [byte[]]::new(1MB)) } }; $jobs += Start-Job { Get-ChildItem C:\ -Recurse -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Out-Null }; $jobs | Wait-Job -Timeout 300 | Out-Null
acpi-s3-under-io.note: VERIFIED 2026-08-27: No crash. Guest agent now installed and responding, ACPI S3 enabled in domain XML, but Windows Server 2025 reports 'suspend-to-ram not supported by OS'. Server editions disable S3 sleep by default. The suspend never executed. Heavy I/O workload ran for 535s without crashing.

poison-msr-pat.name: Page Attribute Table MSR corruption
poison-msr-pat.guestWorkload: Get-ChildItem C:\ -Recurse -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Out-Null; Get-Process | Out-Null; 1..100 | ForEach-Object { [IO.File]::WriteAllBytes("C:\chaos-msr-$_.dat", [byte[]]::new(1MB)) }
poison-msr-pat.note: VERIFIED 2026-08-27: Blocked by security posture. QMP msrwrite absent from QEMU 10.2.2. Host-side kvm-msr-write.py (pidfd_getfd + KVM_SET_MSRS) works but needs sudo (QEMU runs as uid 107). Guest-side NtSystemDebugControl SysDbgWriteMsr returns STATUS_NOT_IMPLEMENTED on Server 2025. CrashMe driver WRMSR IOCTL added but new binary blocked by CI policy (driversipolicy.p7b). Unblock requires one of: (1) sudo access for kvm-msr-write.py, (2) osslsigncode to sign the updated driver, (3) removal of driversipolicy.p7b in the baseline.

tsc-skew-inject.name: TSC offset sudden jump
tsc-skew-inject.note: VERIFIED 2026-08-27: Blocked by same security posture as poison-msr-pat. All three approaches (QMP, host-side KVM ioctl, guest-side CrashMe WRMSR) blocked. High crash potential if any unblock path succeeds.
